issues.summary: [QB-01] Repository filenames can execute shell commands
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-01.
- **Severity:** Critical · **Evidence:** Reproduced · **Phase:** 1 · **Effort:** S
- **Code at review:** context/git.js : 18

## Problem
A repository filename is interpolated into an execSync shell string. Double quotes do not neutralize shell command substitution. A harmless filename probe created a marker during context collection, before any coding agent ran.

## Implement
1. Replace shell strings with execFile/spawn argument arrays and shell:false.
2. Preserve the -- path separator.
3. Audit all subprocess calls for interpolation and reject paths outside the selected repository.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
A filename containing shell metacharacters is treated as a literal path; no marker is created. Spaces, quotes, newlines, and leading hyphens are handled without command execution.

## Where it stands (2026-10-02)
- **Status:** In Review
- **Done so far:** All git and test subprocesses run with argv arrays and shell:false via lib/proc.js; a static test forbids shell-string subprocess calls (test/unit/no-shell-subprocess.test.js).
- **Commits (branch phase-0-1-hardening):** 6258295
- **Evidence / regression tests:** test/unit/qb01-shell-injection.test.js
- **Remaining:** Senior security sign-off.

## Closure (review template, p.33)
Implementation: owner, commit, affected files, migration notes. Evidence: failing pre-fix reproduction, passing regression, CI run, integration evidence where relevant, docs updated. Review: senior sign-off, remaining limitations, closure date.

issues.summary: [QB-02] Agent execution has no enforced containment
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-02.
- **Severity:** High · **Evidence:** Code / design · **Phase:** 1 · **Effort:** L
- **Code at review:** agent/runner.js : 54; bench/baseline.js : 17

## Problem
Claude is started in the supplied repository with --dangerously-skip-permissions and inherited environment. Agent edits, repository scripts, and prompt injection can reach resources outside the intended task. Existing tests and package scripts are writable by the agent.

## Implement
1. Run in a disposable clone inside an OS/container sandbox.
2. Allow only required environment variables, credentials, mounts, and egress.
3. Keep policy, trusted tests, and grading outside the writable checkout; document the threat model.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
A fixture attempting a host-file write, forbidden network request, and trusted-test modification is denied. The user checkout and its Git metadata remain unchanged. A senior engineer approves the boundary.

## Where it stands (2026-10-02)
- **Status:** In Progress
- **Done so far:** Design history: v1 rejected (2026-10-02). v2: changes requested; implementation spikes approved. v3: approved as the working design for experiments E1-E4 and incremental implementation. v3.1 applies the eight targeted corrections from the v3 review (4370778). Separately landed (140020a): the README and CLI banner warning that execution is uncontained and runs with the user's privileges; removal of the production QB_AGENT_COMMAND host-execution override.
- **Commits (branch phase-0-1-hardening):** d9221cf, d03a2b0, 4370778, 140020a
- **Evidence / regression tests:** docs/security/agent-sandbox.md (design); test/unit/qb02-no-agent-override.test.js
- **Remaining:** Run E1 (auth), E2 (tmpfs storage), E3 (Squid networking) and E4 (lifecycle supervisor) on Linux x86_64 + Docker Engine, recording versions, commands, sanitised output and pass/fail per criterion. Fold the results into the design, implement the sandbox, and pass the §11.2 integration suite. Before beta: the §5.5 authentication-obligations check for subscription mode. Done-when not yet met: no host-write, egress or trusted-test-modification fixture exists against a real boundary.
- **Blocker:** Needs a Linux + Docker Engine host (the dev machine is macOS). E1 needs a real Claude subscription login.

## Closure (review template, p.33)
Implementation: owner, commit, affected files, migration notes. Evidence: failing pre-fix reproduction, passing regression, CI run, integration evidence where relevant, docs updated. Review: senior sign-off, remaining limitations, closure date.

issues.summary: [QB-03] Change capture omits parts of the actual result
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-03.
- **Severity:** High · **Evidence:** Reproduced · **Phase:** 1 · **Effort:** M
- **Code at review:** agent/runner.js : 73; bench/baseline.js : 37

## Problem
Bare git diff captures only unstaged tracked changes. New files, staged edits, and agent-created commits can be invisible. A fixture with a staged edit and a new file produced an empty captured diff.

## Implement
1. Pin a trusted base revision before execution.
2. Capture the complete final state in the isolated checkout, including untracked files and changes relative to that base.
3. Use NUL-safe path handling and record renames, deletions, binary changes, modes, and symlinks.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
Fixtures covering staged, unstaged, new, committed, renamed, deleted, binary, and unusual-path changes are captured or explicitly rejected as unsupported. No partial capture can receive PASS.

## Where it stands (2026-10-02)
- **Status:** Sent Back
- **Done so far:** 5019dc4 replaced bare git diff with full tree-snapshot capture (staged, unstaged, new, committed, renamed, deleted, binary, mode, symlink, unusual paths), and it went to review. Reopened during the QB-02 v2 revision: host-side capture runs git against the agent-written .git/config, so an agent-written core.fsmonitor, or a clean filter plus .gitattributes, executes on the host. Confirmed by the QB-02 v2 review. 5107056 adds executable reproductions: two KNOWN DEFECT tests that pass while each attack still fires, with the matching security regressions held as todo.
- **Commits (branch phase-0-1-hardening):** 5019dc4, 5107056
- **Evidence / regression tests:** test/unit/qb03-qb22-capture-and-states.test.js; test/unit/hostile-tree-seeds.test.js
- **Remaining:** The fix is the capture container with a trusted GIT_DIR and a fresh candidate index (agent-sandbox.md §6). Then delete the KNOWN DEFECT tests, un-todo the regressions, and add the §6 fidelity fixtures (deletions, file<->dir, .gitignore-hidden files, CRLF/binary/mode/symlink).
- **Blocker:** Blocked by QB-02 (the §6 capture is part of the sandbox implementation).

## Closure (review template, p.33)
Implementation: owner, commit, affected files, migration notes. Evidence: failing pre-fix reproduction, passing regression, CI run, integration evidence where relevant, docs updated. Review: senior sign-off, remaining limitations, closure date.

issues.summary: [QB-04] Model output can overwrite trusted metadata
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-04.
- **Severity:** High · **Evidence:** Reproduced · **Phase:** 1 · **Effort:** S
- **Code at review:** intent/compiler.js : 108; intent/schema.js : 9; qb.js : 264

## Problem
The compiler spreads model output after its own id, timestamp, and raw_request. A mocked response replaced the original request and set id to ../../model-chosen-location. The artifact path then resolved outside the intended contract directory.

## Implement
1. Parse only allowed semantic fields from the model.
2. Generate trusted metadata after validation and never accept it from model output.
3. Validate artifact identifiers and verify resolved output paths stay beneath the artifact root.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
Injected id, repo_path, created_at, and raw_request values cannot override application metadata. Traversal identifiers cannot write outside the designated run directory.

## Where it stands (2026-10-02)
- **Status:** In Review
- **Done so far:** Model output can no longer set contract id, timestamps, raw_request or repo_path; artifact identifiers are validated and output paths are confined (lib/fsafe.js).
- **Commits (branch phase-0-1-hardening):** 14fdc49
- **Evidence / regression tests:** test/unit/qb04-trusted-metadata.test.js
- **Remaining:** Senior sign-off.

issues.summary: [QB-05] Benchmark reset is destructive and not reproducible
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-05.
- **Severity:** High · **Evidence:** Code-confirmed · **Phase:** 1 · **Effort:** M
- **Code at review:** bench/run.js : 218; bench/tasks.json : 2

## Problem
The harness runs checkout and clean in a hard-coded working repository and swallows errors. It can discard a developer's changes, does not restore a pinned commit or staged state, and leaves ignored files and external state behind.

## Implement
1. Accept an explicit repository plus base revision.
2. Create a disposable checkout per arm and task.
3. Reset database/service/cache fixtures explicitly and fail on setup errors; never clean the supplied working tree.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
Start with dirty tracked, staged, untracked, and ignored files in the source checkout. The harness preserves them all and produces identical initial snapshots for both arms, even after an agent commit.

## Where it stands (2026-10-02)
- **Status:** In Review
- **Done so far:** Benchmark arms run in disposable workspaces pinned to an explicit repo and base revision (lib/workspace.js). A dirty source checkout (tracked, staged, untracked, ignored) is preserved byte-for-byte, and both arms start from identical snapshots even after an agent commit.
- **Commits (branch phase-0-1-hardening):** df4ced7
- **Evidence / regression tests:** test/unit/qb05-bench-workspace.test.js

issues.summary: [QB-06] Test-command failure can still produce PASS
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-06.
- **Severity:** Critical · **Evidence:** Reproduced · **Phase:** 2 · **Effort:** M
- **Code at review:** verify/checker.js : 33; verify/verifier.js : 60

## Problem
Nonzero exits and runner failures are converted into parsed output counts. A command exiting 2 yielded zero failed tests; affirmative judge responses then produced PASS. Missing runners, timeouts, and unrecognized formats are not distinct outcomes.

## Implement
1. Preserve exit code, signal, timeout, duration, and raw evidence.
2. Use a runner adapter with machine-readable results.
3. Treat runner error, missing required tests, and zero unexpected tests as verification errors that cannot approve a task.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
Exit 2, timeout, missing executable, collection failure, malformed report, and zero-test fixtures never pass. A real failing test is distinguished from infrastructure failure.

issues.description:

- **Severity:** Critical · **Evidence:** Reproduced · **Phase:** 2 · **Effort:** S
- **Code at review:** verify/judge.js : 194

## Problem
The prose fallback searches for words such as implemented and true. The response "The criterion is not implemented." was parsed as true on all three controlled calls.

## Implement
1. Require a strict judgment schema with a boolean-or-null field and structured evidence references.
2. Delete keyword-to-verdict fallbacks.
3. Classify malformed output separately; allow at most a bounded format retry without turning it into evidence.

issues.summary: [QB-08] An empty or clarification-only contract can pass
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-08.
- **Severity:** Critical · **Evidence:** Reproduced · **Phase:** 2 · **Effort:** S
- **Code at review:** verify/verifier.js : 30; qb.js : 75; bench/run.js : 115

## Problem
verify() defaults missing criteria to an empty array. With a nonempty diff and no blocking tests, the empty array produces PASS. The benchmark does not handle a clarifying response; root handling also does not recheck a second clarification.

## Implement
1. Validate contract type and nonempty, unique requirements at every boundary.
2. Use an explicit needs_clarification state.
3. Prevent agent execution and verification until a finalized contract exists; expose that state cleanly in noninteractive mode.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
Empty ACs, missing goal, duplicate IDs, a first clarification, and a second clarification never execute the agent or return PASS. Tests cover CLI and benchmark entry points.

issues.summary: [QB-09] Scope and constraints are not enforced as policy
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-09.
- **Severity:** High · **Evidence:** Reproduced · **Phase:** 2 · **Effort:** M
- **Code at review:** verify/checker.js : 105; verify/verifier.js : 47; agent/briefing.js : 52

## Problem
Scope violations are included in the report but do not block PASS. Constraints only appear in the briefing unless also represented as ACs. Relevant files are treated as an apparent allowlist even though retrieval confidence is not authorization.

## Implement
1. Separate relevant_files from allowed_changes and protected_paths.
2. Convert enforceable constraints into policy checks.
3. Block forbidden edits and require an explicit policy update for legitimate scope expansion.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
A forbidden file change blocks PASS even when every judge vote is positive. A newly relevant file is not silently authorized, and each declared constraint maps to evidence or an explicit unresolved item.

## Where it stands (2026-10-02)
- **Status:** To Do
- **Remaining:** All implementation work. Starts after the Phase 1 gate.

issues.summary: [QB-10] Failure routing loses test failures and repair actions
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-10.
- **Severity:** High · **Evidence:** Reproduced · **Phase:** 2 · **Effort:** M
- **Code at review:** verify/verifier.js : 54; qb.js : 176; bench/run.js : 168

## Problem
Failed tests only override a pass verdict. Failed tests plus unknown ACs produce partial. With all ACs true, failed tests produce fail but no AC failures or repair hints, so the loop stops. No baseline test run proves that a failure is pre-existing.

## Implement
1. Aggregate policy, execution, test, and semantic outcomes independently.
2. Create repair actions from concrete test failures.
3. Compare base and candidate test evidence and route infrastructure errors to environment recovery, not code repair.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
A newly failing regression enters a bounded repair with its test evidence. A known base failure stays visible. Unknown ACs cannot hide a definite failure, and unchanged patches do not restart endless repairs.

## Where it stands (2026-10-02)
- **Status:** To Do
- **Remaining:** All implementation work. Starts after the Phase 1 gate.

Implementation: owner, commit, affected files, migration notes. Evidence: failing pre-fix reproduction, passing regression, CI run, integration evidence where relevant, docs updated. Review: senior sign-off, remaining limitations, closure date.

issues.description:

## Problem

2. Assign immutable evidence IDs with file hashes and ranges.
3. Report truncation and missing evidence explicitly; never present partial input as complete.

issues.description:

## Problem
A comment mentioning the target, a commented export, and an unrelated return statement set defined/exported/returns to true. Keyword scanning also examines deleted and context lines. These are text hints presented as high-confidence facts.

1. Parse supported-language syntax and resolve the actual symbol and binding.
2. Keep heuristic matches labeled as search hints.
3. Do not use absence from added lines as evidence that an unchanged implementation is absent.

issues.summary: [QB-15] Voting and preservation rules are not calibrated
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-15.
- **Severity:** High · **Evidence:** Design risk · **Phase:** 2 · **Effort:** M
- **Code at review:** verify/judge.js : 18; verify/judge.js : 142

## Problem
Identical low-temperature calls share blind spots and missing evidence. Repeated attempts can change the vote without changing code. Changing preservation ACs to null avoids a false repair but leaves partial, not verified success.

## Implement
1. Make preservation claims bounded to named tests/interfaces.
2. Calibrate verdicts against independently labeled patches and report abstention.
3. Cache evidence by patch hash and measure whether extra votes outperform one judge at equal cost.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
An unchanged patch does not become approved by repeated resampling alone. False acceptance, false rejection, and abstention are measured separately. No rule treats null as proof of preservation.

## Where it stands (2026-10-02)
- **Status:** To Do
- **Remaining:** All implementation work. Starts after the Phase 1 gate.

issues.summary: [QB-38] Runs lack a durable, versioned evidence record
issues.description:
- **Source:** Engineering Review v1.0 (reviewed snapshot 4ecc6a7, 1 Oct 2026), ticket QB-38.
- **Severity:** High · **Evidence:** Code-confirmed · **Phase:** 0 · **Effort:** M
- **Code at review:** qb.js : 99; qb.js : 156; qb.js : 209; bench/run.js : 175

## Problem
Artifacts are optional and spread across layer directories. There is no authoritative run manifest connecting the base snapshot, accepted requirements, attempts, check execution, model settings, and final decision. This prevents diagnosis, replay, and audit.

## Implement
1. Define versioned run, requirement, check, attempt, and evidence schemas.
2. Persist a manifest and append-only events by default in a controlled run directory.
3. Add checksums, redaction, explicit retention, and crash-safe writes; keep migrations documented.

## Done when (acceptance criteria)
One run ID retrieves the complete decision trail without relying on console output. A crashed run resumes or terminates explicitly. Replaying verdict aggregation on the stored evidence reproduces the recorded outcome.

- **Status:** In Review
- **Done so far:** Versioned run manifest and append-only evidence record in one run directory; qb replay/runs/show; interrupted runs are closed as ABANDONED or ERROR on the next start.
